380YE Winter Solstice Imperial elections.d: New senators were chosen for Miekarova (Father Nikolovich Drakov), Sarvos (Magdelena di Sarvos), Karov (Ludmilla Koslov) and Therunin (Willa Farkus-Vigil), while other seats returned their incumbents. New generals were Nikolai Zakharovich Prochnost, Iron Osric, Natalia Barossa, Akstis Eigulys (a reduced term to Spring 381YE) and Cayleb. In the Synod, Ricardo Almieda Desmondo di Tassatto became Cardinal of Prosperity and Ingrid Sigeing Conscience of the Senate. The Conclave gained new Archmages of Night, Day and Spring and a new Grandmaster of the Rod and Shield. The Imperial Censor was open for election for the first time. Bourse seats went to various bidders, including Siliva Alcham, who paid 200 thrones for the Great Mine of Briante.

n.Dawn: Dawn returned its incumbents as Senator for Astolat and as General of the Hounds of Glory.
n.Highguard: Highguard kept its incumbent Senator for Necropolis, Cayleb became General of the Valiant Pegasus, and Nemuel of Ravensfell won the Great Forest at Reikos.
n.Imperial Orcs: The Imperial Orcs returned their incumbents as Senator for Skarsind and as General of the Winter Sun.
n.Navarr: Willa Farkus-Vigil became Senator for Therunin, Hercynia kept its incumbent, and Morgan Leafstalker of Navarr became Gatekeeper of Prosperity.
n.The Brass Coast: The Brass Coast returned its incumbents as Senator for Madruga and as Admiral of the Freeborn Storm navy.
n.The League: Magdelena di Sarvos became Senator for Sarvos and Natalia Barossa General of the Towerjacks, while Ricardo Almieda Desmondo di Tassatto of the League became Cardinal of Prosperity; Temeschwar kept its incumbent senator.
n.The Marches: The Marches returned their incumbents as Senator for Bregasland and as General of the Strong Reeds.
n.Urizen: Urizen's incumbent Senator for Zenith was returned.
n.Varushka: Varushka gained new senators for Miekarova and Karov, new generals for the Army of the Golden Axe and, for a reduced term, the Iron Helms, and Amris of Varushka became Gatekeeper of Wisdom.
n.Wintermark: Iron Osric became General of the Green Shield Army, Ingrid Sigeing of Wintermark became Conscience of the Senate, and Kallavesa kept its incumbent senator.

t.Karov: Ludmilla Koslov was elected Senator for Karov.
t.Miekarova: Father Nikolovich Drakov was elected Senator for Miekarova.
t.Reikos: The Bourse seat for the Great Forest at Reikos went to Nemuel of Ravensfell for a bid of 56 thrones.
t.Sarvos: Magdelena di Sarvos was elected Senator for Sarvos.
t.Therunin: Willa Farkus-Vigil was elected Senator for Therunin.

380YE Winter Solstice winds of fortune.d: The Synod faced a possible schism over the Congregation of the First Empress, and the stars vanished across the Empire. The Stalker was diverted from Miekarova and struck eastern Otkodov, where the Thule offered to share its ilium. The people of Whittle fled Jotun rule for Tassato Mestra. Gaunt figures haunted the Metri, the orcs of the Mallum offered peace talks over the Barrens, and Dogri Thulebane prepared something in Crow's Ridge. The Bourse private auction collapsed. Ennerlund became marsh, reducing Holberg's farms and raising upkeep on the Great Pits. The Court of the White Fountain's curse ended, and Lashonar's heralds were countered in Dawn.

n.Dawn: Dawn was tagged in the Druj offer to negotiate peace over the Barrens and faced bandits allied with renegade witches near Applefell. Lady Tamain Sepulchre's song The Heralds of Lashonar had entirely countered the eternal's influence on Dawn's armies by the Solstice.
n.Druj: The orcs of the Mallum offered to negotiate peace with the Empire over the Barrens and the situation in the east.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: a Grendel attack is named as one thing that could hinder the recovery of the Court of the White Fountain in Optarion.
n.Highguard: Highguard, especially its benefactors, was flagged as affected by the collapse of the Bourse private auction. It was also tagged in the transfer of Empress Giselle's sarcophagus to Temeschwar.
n.Imperial Orcs: The Imperial Orcs were tagged in the collapse of the Bourse private auction and in the Stalker's fall in Otkodov. They were also named as one possible holder of the Krampus's uncertain allegiance.
n.Jotun: Renewed Jotun domination of the Mourn drove the people of Whittle to abandon their homes en masse. The Jotun were also named as one possible holder of the Krampus's allegiance.
n.Navarr: The orcs of the Great Forest still occupied the Lower Tarn Valley in Therunin, and the question of land remained foremost for many Navarr of the south-east.
n.The Brass Coast: The Asavean temple in Oran neared completion, raising the question of the Asavean counter-offer to build a temple in Nemoria. The Brass Coast was also tagged in the collapse of the Bourse private auction.
n.The League: The League received the Whittle refugees in Tassato Mestra and faced gaunt figures in Temeschwar's Metri. Ennerlund's transformation into marsh permanently reduced Holberg's farms, while Giselle's sarcophagus lay beneath Ratibor's Gate and work on the Blood Red Roads continued.
n.The Marches: The Marches were tagged in the exodus of the people of Whittle in the Mourn, who fled south under renewed Jotun domination.
n.Thule: The Stalker crashed into eastern Otkodov, and the Thule offered the Empire an arrangement to share in its ilium, as previously agreed, though the Dragons' dealings were said never to be straightforward.
n.Urizen: The curse on the Court of the White Fountain in Optarion ran its course after one final season of damage, and its fire flared up again. Spiral's citizens were flagged as concerned by the season's magical effects.
n.Varushka: Varushka was tagged in the Stalker's diversion from Miekarova and was offered the golden hare as a new candidate Virtuous Animal. Disruptive weather kept the upkeep of the Icy Crag of the Eternal Sun artificially high.
n.Wintermark: Dogri Thulebane of Crow's Ridge was preparing something that could affect the northern Empire, and strange hunters kept raiding Sermersuaq. The Krampus behaved erratically with its allegiance unclear, and Wintermark was tagged in the Bourse auction's collapse.

t.Bregasland: Mentioned in passing: it is cited as one of the great marshes of the west, alongside which Holberg's enlarged marsh now ranks.
t.Feroz: The Asavean temple in Oran was nearing completion despite some opposition from the Synod, and its priest and builders were seeking a new challenge.
t.Holberg: Ennerlund finished turning into marsh, permanently reducing the territory's farm production by 36 rings and raising the Great Pits' upkeep by 2 Thrones a season.
t.Kallavesa: Mentioned in passing: it is cited as one of the great marshes of the west, alongside which Holberg's enlarged marsh now ranks.
t.Miekarova: The falling Stalker was diverted at the last moment away from Miekarova, striking Otkodov instead.
t.Mournwold: The people of Whittle left their homes en masse under renewed Jotun domination, travelling south with all their possessions.
t.Otkodov: The Stalker smashed into eastern Otkodov, its supernatural influence faded, and the Thule offered the Empire a share of the ilium it contains.
t.Redoubt: The curse on the Court of the White Fountain in Optarion ended after a last season of attack, leaving the tower's fire restored but its white stone still cracked.
t.Reikos: Mentioned in passing: its citizens are flagged as concerned by the season's round-up of magical effects, which is not detailed here.
t.Sermersuaq: Raids by strange hunters continued to disrupt businesses and farms, with Savik Summerstorm coordinating efforts to learn more.
t.Skarsind: Dogri Thulebane in Crow's Ridge was preparing something of wide impact. No progress was made on building a home for the Krampus in the territory.
t.Spiral: Mentioned in passing: its citizens are flagged as concerned by the season's round-up of magical effects, which is not detailed here.
t.Tassato: The people of Whittle arrived seeking sanctuary in Tassato Mestra after fleeing the Jotun-dominated Mourn.
t.Temeschwar: Gaunt figures in the Metri slaughtered anyone attempting violence against a citizen. Empress Giselle's sarcophagus was stored beneath Ratibor's Gate to await its new tomb.
t.The Barrens: The orcs of the Mallum offered to negotiate peace with the Empire over the Barrens and the situation in the east.
t.Therunin: The orcs of the Great Forest continued to occupy the Lower Tarn Valley. Senator Caerwyn Summer Crow provided them with money and supplies, but the question of land remained unresolved.
t.Weirwater: Bandits allied with renegade witches attacked a weirwood caravan near Applefell, the latest in an escalating series of problems with witches in southern Weirwater.

r.Feroz/Oranseri: The Asavean temple in Oran was largely complete, opening the question of an Asavean counter-offer to build a temple in Nemoria.
r.Holberg/Ennerlund: Ennerlund completed its slow transformation into marsh, and its Great Pits now need extra pumps and precautions that raise their upkeep by 2 Thrones a season.
r.Holberg/Rebeshof: Mentioned in passing: Rebeshof is part of the enlarged marsh that Ennerlund has now joined.
r.Holberg/The Morass: Mentioned in passing: the Morass is part of the enlarged marsh that Ennerlund has now joined.
r.Mournwold/Freemoor: The people of Whittle travelled south through the Freemoor hills with all their possessions on their way to Tassato Mestra.
r.Redoubt/Optarion: The curse on the Court of the White Fountain ended and its fire flared up again, though cracks in the tower's white stone still need repair.
r.Skarsind/Crow’s Ridge: Dogri Thulebane, renegade leader of the Winterfolk here, was preparing something whose impact may be felt across the northern Empire and beyond.
r.Tassato/Tassato Mestra: The people of Whittle arrived here seeking sanctuary after fleeing the Mourn.
r.Temeschwar/Metri: Something cold and dark settled over the woods, where gaunt figures slaughtered anyone bringing violence to another citizen, leaving the roads safer but the woods darker.
r.Therunin/Lower Tarn Valley: The orcs of the Great Forest, seeking sanctuary from the Barrens, continued to occupy the valley, with little change from the previous season.

380YE Winter Solstice winds of war.d: Spiral, Necropolis, Reikos and Weirwater saw no major fighting, though the army of the dead lingered in Weirwater's forests. In the Mournwold both sides held their ground, and the Jotun freed branded Marcher 'oathbreakers' with a warning of no more mercy. Four Imperial armies stormed a Summer-realm citadel to free Serra Damata, losing around a hundred soldiers. The Golden Sun and Gryphon's Pride took Murderdale. Orcs seized about a third of Naris and sent raiders toward Elos and Evenstar. The Black Thorns lost Beacon Point and were boxed into Western Scout. Five Sentinel Gate conjunctions were identified in Redoubt, Liathaven and the Mournwold.

n.Dawn: The Golden Sun and Gryphon's Pride consolidated Carmine Fields and took Murderdale with few casualties, helped by a field hospital, while Dawnish knights errant fought the unliving host in Weirwater.
n.Druj: The Druj seemed to continue their conquest in the Barrens and possibly fought the briar heretics at Dourfell Keep, but avoided the Dawnish amid rumours of secret compacts.
n.Grendel: The Grendel held southern Spiral and the Black Plateau without seeking battle, and their mariners supported a landing of mostly Lasambrian orcs in southern Redoubt.
n.Highguard: The Highborn began rebuilding chapters among the new forests of Reikos, while the Quiet Step kept watch over Necropolis's coast against a Grendel assault that never came.
n.Jotun: The Jotun abandoned Kahraman behind a Summer citadel, then slaughtered three thousand Black Thorns in Liathaven and freed branded Mourn oathbreakers with a message that there would be no more mercy.
n.Navarr: The Black Thorns, swollen past seven thousand, lost three thousand soldiers and Beacon Point to the Jotun and were left trapped in Western Scout with only hard options for escape.
n.The Brass Coast: The Fire of the South helped liberate Serra Damata, restoring all of Kahraman and the Damatian Cliffs granite to the Empire, while the Red Wind Corsairs stood vigil in Necropolis.
n.The League: The Towerjacks joined the liberation of Serra Damata, while League generals urged their troops to rest and prepare for the war ahead.
n.The Marches: The Marches kept Greensward and buried their dead, while nearly a hundred Mourn folk branded as oathbreakers were released into Graven Marsh; the Singing Caves remained unallocated after a Throne veto.
n.Urizen: Spires in Ankra and Cinion began rebuilding, but in Redoubt the Heliopticon raised the alarm as orcs looted spires in Naris and threatened Elos and the hospital spire of Evenstar.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: the army of the dead lingering in Weirwater originally emerged from Karsk.

t.Astolat: Mentioned in passing: the unquiet dead had earlier been driven back from Astolat.
t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: Quiet Step scouts watched the bay from the Necropolis cliffs for signs of a naval invasion.
t.Bregasland: Nearly a hundred branded Mourn folk crossed from Grey March into Graven Marsh, watched by five hundred silent Jotun on the hills above High Courage.
t.Kahraman: With Serra Damata liberated after a three-day siege of a Summer citadel, all of Kahraman was back under Imperial control.
t.Karsk: Mentioned in passing: the undead army now in Weirwater had emerged from Karsk six months earlier.
t.Liathaven: A Jotun host from Kahraman destroyed the Black Thorns' gains, retook Beacon Point and left the army trapped in the west of the territory.
t.Mournwold: No fighting took place; the Empire held Greensward, the Jotun held the rest, and a conjunction offered a chance to learn the Jotun's western plans.
t.Necropolis: The Quiet Step and Red Wind Corsairs guarded Sanctuary Sands and built an unlit warning beacon by the tomb of Atuman, but no Grendel attack came.
t.Redoubt: Lasambrian orcs backed by Grendel ships landed in the south, looted spires and threatened Elos and Evenstar, with two Sentinel Gate conjunctions opening to meet them.
t.Reikos: With the Spring magic subsided, Highborn rebuilding began among new forests, though Llofir's Tamarbode stayed silent and eerie mushroom light glowed beneath the trees.
t.Reinos: Mentioned in passing: an advance south into Reinos was one possible escape route for the trapped Black Thorns.
t.Segura: Mentioned in passing: Black Thorns losses were compared to the dead of the Iron Plains, and the Lasambrian invaders were said to come from beyond Segura.
t.Spiral: Imperial and Grendel forces each defended their own ground with only scout skirmishes, while Ankra and Cinion began to rebuild.
t.Tassato: Mentioned in passing: sentries on the walls of La Redotta Rezia kept a nervous watch for an orc return that did not come.
t.The Barrens: Dawnish armies now held Murderdale, Carmine Fields and Dawnguard, while the Druj moved elsewhere in the territory without engaging them.
t.The Semmerlak: Mentioned in passing: the undead host now in Weirwater had come out of the Semmerlak.
t.Weirwater: The army of the dead remained in the forests, drawing knights errant to fight it, while missing pedlars and woodcutters fuelled cries that someone must do something.

r.Kahraman/Serra Damata: Four Imperial armies stormed the Summer citadel and freed Damata, recovering the white granite of the Damatian Cliffs and finding a Jotun promise carved on the walls to return.
r.Liathaven/Beacon Point: The Jotun overran the Black Thorns left to hold Beacon Point and retook it within a month.
r.Liathaven/West Ranging: This Jotun-held region was a possible refuge for the Black Thorns if they crossed the vallorn by the Paths of Lan Thúven.
r.Liathaven/Western Scout: The Black Thorns retook ruined steadings here and still clung to parts of the region as a beachhead, though now under Jotun attack.
r.Mournwold/Greensward: Retaken by the Empire, Greensward was held without fighting as Marcher dead were buried in its south-eastern farms.
r.Redoubt/Naris: Invading orcs seized Rebekah's Leap and about a third of Naris, looting spires and sending raiders toward Elos and Evenstar.
r.Reikos/Broken Ride: Builders in western Broken Ride saw the faint glow of mushrooms beneath the trees at night.
r.Reikos/Grey Charge: Builders in northern Grey Charge saw an eerie mushroom glow beneath the trees under starless skies.
r.Reikos/Longshire: Builders in north-western Longshire saw the faint luminescent glow of mushrooms in the nearby forest.
r.Reikos/Tamarbode: Tamarbode stayed silent, with no woodcutting or quarrying in the dark forest claimed by Llofir.
r.Segura/Iron Plains: Mentioned in passing: the Black Thorns' losses were said to exceed those suffered on the Iron Plains.
r.Spiral/Ankra: Spires in Ankra began slowly to rebuild amid only scattered scout skirmishes.
r.Spiral/Cinion: Spires in Cinion began slowly to rebuild as the front stayed quiet.
r.The Barrens/Dawnguard: Mentioned in passing: Dawnguard remained among the Dawnish holdings in the Barrens.
r.The Barrens/Murderdale: Dawnish armies swept aside disorganised orc resistance and took Murderdale, leaving survivors to turn to banditry in the woods.
r.Weirwater/Hawksmoor: The unquiet dead still lurked in Hawksmoor's forests, where corpselights danced and travellers went missing.
r.Weirwater/Weirmoor: The undead host remained in Weirmoor's woods, drawing questing knights to deadly fights.

A business like any other.d: With Kantor's port open, Axou traders brought spices, narcotics, orichalcum and bone carvings, with a few closed-mouthed Skouran passengers. They sought metalwork, dragonbone, green iron and liao, so liao sold for 20 rings instead of 12 this season. The Synod or Senate could encourage or restrict that trade. Jarm lifted its last sanctions, giving bonuses at Kavor, Vezak and Rigia if relations held through the Solstice. A Suranni faction offered to open Robec for a bribe. Faraden caravans flourished. Sarcophan stayed neutral while a white granite dock began at Cargo. Sumaah still held the Imperial Crown and remained at war, the Commonwealth stayed chilly and Thule showed cautious interest in trade.

n.Dawn: Adventurous Axou captains braved the Semmerlak to trade in Dawn. Starac Sijed Orzel of House Orzel, Ambassador to the Iron Confederacy, was expected to learn the details of the Robec proposal first.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: Grendel vessels were regular visitors to the Sarcophan Delves' southern port, which kept open diplomatic relations with them.
n.Highguard: Axou merchants on the Bay of Catazar favoured other nations' ports over those of Highguard. The skeletal Sumaah embassy in Necropolis continued its quiet business.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: a binding treaty with the Faraden let their caravans pass through the northern Lasambrian hills unmolested by the Jotun.
n.The Brass Coast: Brass Coast ports were among those Axou merchants favoured, and Feroz mazzarine was on sale in Sarvos. Reports from southern Feroz revealed a Suranni fortification being built in Kalino.
n.The League: League ports drew Axou trade, and a Sarvos shopkeeper was shown selling liao to Axou buyers. There were rumours of Jarmish interest in the Tassato Mana Exchange.
n.The Marches: Mentioned in passing: Senator Henry Ward of Upwold was quoted for the Senate statement welcoming trade with Jarm.
n.Thule: The Thule orcs expressed cautious interest in establishing an embassy and opening trade routes with the northern Empire.
n.Urizen: Urizen ports were favoured by Axou merchants. Work began on a loading dock at Cargo that, once completed, will let a chosen minister purchase Sarcophan white granite.
n.Varushka: Axou captains crossed the Semmerlak to trade in Varushka, and Volodmartz bladeroot featured among the herbs sold in Sarvos.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: the Sarvos shopkeeper in the story offered 'special' herbs supposedly shipped from Kallavesa.

t.Bay of Catazar: Black-sailed Axou merchants plied the Bay in significant numbers, favouring Brass Coast, League and Urizen ports over those of Highguard.
t.Feroz: Mazzarine from the Feroz Spice Gardens was traded abroad. Reports from southern Feroz told of a significant Suranni fortification going up across the border in Kalino.
t.Kalino: The Suranni began work on a significant fortification in Kalino, overlooking a main route through the southern Lasambrian Hills to the Iron Confederacy heartland.
t.Kallavesa: Mentioned in passing: a shopkeeper in the story claimed a shipment of 'special' herbs from Kallavesa.
t.Necropolis: Mentioned in passing: the skeletal staff of the Sumaah embassy in Necropolis conducted their little business with a minimum of fuss.
t.Redoubt: Work began on a loading dock at the international trade port of Cargo, under a treaty with a Sarcophan Bedelaar-Huisbaas, to allow purchases of white granite once completed.
t.Sarvos: In the story, a Sarvos herb shop was visited by Axou necromancer and guard seeking to buy as much liao as the shopkeeper had, a sign of the city's new Axou trade.
t.Tassato: Mentioned in passing: there was a rumour of Jarmish interest in the Tassato Mana Exchange.
t.The Semmerlak: Adventurous Axou captains were reported braving the Semmerlak to reach Varushka and Dawn.
t.Upwold: Mentioned in passing: the quoted Senate statement on trade with Jarm was attributed to Senator Henry Ward of Upwold.
t.Volodmartz: Mentioned in passing: a shipment of Volodmartz bladeroot was on sale in the Sarvos shop in the story.

Allocate the Singing Caves II.d: After the Empire recovered the Singing Caves in Mournwold, an earlier motion to allocate them fell to the veto of Empress Lisabetta. This second motion, proposed by the senator for Upwold and seconded by the senator for Mitwold, was raised in Winter 380YE and passed as an Imperial motion. As a result, the Singing Caves became an Imperial bourse position, and the seat was auctioned at the Winter Solstice 380YE for a reduced term.

n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun are not named on the page; they are linked only because they held Mournwold, where the caves lie, that season.

t.Mournwold: The Singing Caves in Mournwold, recovered by the Empire, became an Imperial bourse position and were auctioned for a reduced term at the Winter Solstice 380YE.

Archive:380YE Winter Solstice Imperial t.d: The list names the senator for every Imperial territory, along with Senate appointments such as the Conscience of the Senate, Ingrid Sigeing, and ambassadors to foreign nations. It notes that the Senate abrogated the Civilian Commissioners at this Solstice, so those titles no longer exist. It records each nation's generals; the General of the Gryphon's Pride post was vacant after Soldier Akella died at the Solstice, and the Imperial Fleet Master post was also vacant. It also lists the Synod's cardinals and other religious posts, the six Archmagi and Grandmasters, and Bourse seats. The Damatian Cliffs were back under Imperial control and awaited allocation by the Senate.

n.Dawn: Dawn held three Senate seats and several titles, including Cardinal of Wisdom Agnetha de Rondell and Warmage Barthol de Rondell. Its army the Gryphon's Pride was left without a general after Soldier Akella died at the Winter Solstice.
n.Highguard: Highguard held four Senate seats and three generalships, and its people filled many Synod posts, including Imperial Inquisitor Ephron of Adina's Charge and several Virtue Inquisitors and Gatekeepers.
n.Imperial Orcs: The Imperial Orcs were represented by Senator Irontide Vio for Skarsind, Generals Bloodcrow Morgur and Irontide Skar, and Cardinal Atla of the Way. They also held the Steel Fist and the Brilliant Shore on the Bourse.
n.Navarr: Navarr held three Senate seats and two generalships. Brendan Brackensong served as Quartermaster General, and Corwin Leafstalker and Morgan Leafstalker held places in the Synod.
n.The Brass Coast: The Freeborn held four Senate seats and three military commands, including Admiral Edgardo i Ruiloba i Guerra of the Freeborn Storm, along with the Broken Shore Bounty and several Bourse titles.
n.The League: The League held the Throne through Empress Lisabetta Giacomi von Holberg, four Senate seats and four cardinalships. Its citizens held numerous Bourse seats, including the Great Pits of Ennerlund and the Master of the Imperial Mint.
n.The Marches: The Marches held three Senate seats and four generalships. Robert Shanks served as Operator of Brock's Toll, and Tobias Shanks held the Fortress of Salt.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: the Stonefield Ice Caves of Wintermark are noted as held by the Thule.
n.Urizen: Urizen held four Senate seats and a single general, Nicassia Avicia of the Citadel Guard. Its people also held posts including High Exorcist Solas and Cardinal of Courage Levitia of Endsmeet.
n.Varushka: Varushka held four Senate seats, three generalships, the Cardinal of Pride Elka Nadayanova Gremani, and Bourse seats such as the Granites of Veltsgorsk and the Eternal Shafts of Time.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark held three Senate seats and two generalships, and Ingrid Sigeing served as Conscience of the Senate. Its national Stonefield Ice Caves were recorded as held by the Thule.
