Authorise targets of the Imperial Guerdo.d: Dan Brackensong, Quartermaster General of the Imperial Armies, used the power the Senate granted his office to name the season's targets of the Imperial Guerdon. He named the Liathaven Spy Network, the Black Thorns, the Hounds of Glory and the Wolves of War, and closed with a call for a moment of silence for the dead. As a result, owners of military units who supported one of the named armies received a share of the Imperial Guerdon. The motion was approved under the Quartermaster General's own authority, not by a Senate vote.

n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun are not named. The motion only directs the Guerdon to a spy network in Liathaven, a territory the Jotun held at the time.

t.Liathaven: The Liathaven Spy Network was named as a target of the Imperial Guerdon, so Imperial support was directed to the spy operation in this Jotun-held territory.

Beware my power.d: Freeborn magicians raised storms off Spiral that battered shipping in the north-eastern Bay of Catazar and may have hampered Asavean granite shipments to their orc allies. Magical fortifications rose in Kallavesa and Necropolis, though neither was attacked. Sentinel Gate conjunctions behaved oddly, apparently because of the fallen red star. Spring magic healed Cinion and its fire-scarred soldiers, but the overgrowth tore apart ruined spires and damaged Damakan's Forge; one Winter-tainted grove resisted the healing. A surge of healthy, mostly green-eyed babies followed last year's Hallow of the Green World. The Silver Mask persona emerged among the Dawnish. Tamarbode remains under Llofir's control, and the Semmerlak is calm again.

n.Dawn: Dawnish guiser troupes created the Silver Mask, a new minor persona of the Captain, and some Dawnish actors claim it is a real, masked Dawnish figure behind tales of spies and hidden justice.
n.Grendel: Grendel's orcs in the ruins of Apulian may have lost Asavean deliveries of white granite to the storms, and it is unclear whether any Grendel navies in the Bay were battered.
n.Highguard: Magical fortifications rose in the woodlands of Necropolis, and Highborn magisters judged that the Llofir occupying Tamarbode in Reikos is playing a long game.
n.Navarr: Navarr vates agreed that Llofir is interested in the long game, and its servants showed no sign of entering Elerael. Some of the most traditional Navarr voiced concern that the many new green-eyed babies carry the briar lineage.
n.The League: League guisers spread wild tales of an incarnated Silver Mask, and a vindictive play by an anonymous Tassato playwright imagined horrible fates for Guillermo di Tassato.
n.Urizen: Urizen citizens spent three months cutting back the overgrowth that threatened Damakan's Forge in Cinion and saved its central parts. However, the damage means any runeforge project there needs a new costing from the civil service.
n.Wintermark: The Sussivari Frost Coven and Sherard Hunters kept wielding powerful magic for the Empire, and magical castles rose in the marshes of Kallavesa.

t.Bay of Catazar: Freeborn storms battered ships in the north-eastern Bay, and astronomancers sailed out onto its open waters to see the hidden stars.
t.Brocéliande: The servants of Llofir showed no interest in crossing from Tamarbode into Brocéliande's region of Elerael.
t.Kallavesa: Magical fortifications rose in Kallavesa's marshes and would have hindered any attacking army, though no barbarian attack came this season.
t.Necropolis: Magical castles rose in the woodlands of Necropolis, ready to impede attackers, though the territory was not attacked this season.
t.Reikos: Reikos's region of Tamarbode remains under Llofir's control, but its servants showed no interest in exploring the rest of Reikos.
t.Spiral: Massive storms off Spiral's coast hampered shipping from the war-torn territory and Asavean supply runs. Meanwhile, Spring magic healed the fire damage in Cinion but wrecked ruined spires and parts of Damakan's Forge.
t.Tassato: Mentioned in passing: an anonymous Tassato playwright wrote a vindictive Silver Mask play about Guillermo di Tassato, and the page recalls Piero of Both Banks in first-century Tassato.
t.The Semmerlak: The Semmerlak's troubles ended. Its waters turned placid and warm, fisherfolk landed bumper hauls, and its odd folk apologised after the Lady of the Semmerlak was reportedly rescued from a curse.

r.Brocéliande/Elerael: Llofir's servants in neighbouring Tamarbode showed no interest in poking around Elerael.
r.Reikos/Tamarbode: Tamarbode remains under Llofir. Only the mana site of Tamar's Toes is accessible, where gatherers report watchful creatures and mould-infested clothes, and a living fungal castle reportedly still stands at the Sign of Tamar.
r.Spiral/Apulus: The storms probably stymied Asavean vessels carrying white granite to their orc allies in the ruins of Apulian.
r.Spiral/Ateri: A story circulating in Ateri claims at least one Asavean galley was caught by the storm and smashed against the southern cliffs.
r.Spiral/Cinion: Spring magic healed Cinion's fire damage and its injured, but overgrowth destroyed ruined spires including Ossen's Spire and damaged Damakan's Forge. One small burnt grove, infused with Winter magic and possibly a nascent regio, is being watched by illuminates.

City folk and country folk.d: Whittle's thirty-year truce with the Jotun ended after the villagers aided the Empire, and young, old and infirm alike fled to Tassato. Margaret Steward offered green iron for the Rua da Madeira and the Avenida da Penha, a run-down hilltop quarter of Mestra, to house their dependants apart from city life. The fighters would go on to Overton. An enclave was estimated to yield 50 ingots of green iron a season for a year to Tassato's businesses. It also carried the risk of Synod censure, because the Whittlers openly embrace Hatred. The Sheriff of the Mournwold must decide whether Overton accepts their fighters. Friar Robin was travelling to Anvil to face his accusers and to seek an accommodation with the Marcher Assembly.

n.Imperial Orcs: Mentioned in passing: a few orcs at the Mestra docks claimed to be Imperial Orcs, though onlookers doubted it.
n.Jotun: The Jotun ended their long, uneasy truce with Whittle after the villagers aided the Empire, driving the Whittlefolk from their land. The Whittlers now vow to fight them from Overton and to return if their land is retaken.
n.The League: Tassato's Chamber of Commerce, which unites Mestran and Regarian merchants, had to decide whether to sell Mestran streets to the Whittlefolk. It weighed the green iron profit against the risk of Synod condemnation and the spread of Hatred.
n.The Marches: Whittle Marchers were made refugees by the Jotun, and the Sheriff of the Mournwold must decide whether to take their fighters into the Overton garrison. Friar Robin was seeking an accommodation with the Marcher Assembly over the Whittlers' belief in Hatred.

t.Mournwold: The Whittlefolk were forced out of their village in the Mournwold. Their fighters proposed to return to the territory to join the garrison at Overton, pending the Sheriff's approval.
t.Tassato: The refugees camped outside Tassato Mestra and worked its docks. The territory's businesses were offered about 50 green iron ingots a season if the Chamber agreed to an enclave, but the deal carried religious and social risks.

r.Mournwold/Freemoor: The Marcher village of Whittle in Freemoor lost its thirty-year truce with the Jotun, and its people fled south along the old road to Tassato.
r.Mournwold/Greensward: The Whittlers' fighters offered to join the garrison at Overton, though they did not wish to settle their families in the Greensward. Their arrival could spread their Hatred among the garrison.
r.Tassato/Tassato Mestra: The Whittlefolk camped outside Mestra's walls and worked its short-handed docks. They sought to buy the run-down Rua da Madeira and Avenida da Penha as a closed enclave for their dependants.

Construct Alchemical Workshop in Miaren.d: In Winter 380YE the Senate approved the construction of an alchemical workshop, a potion lab dedicated to Murit, in the Navarr territory of Miaren. The motion was proposed by Miaren and seconded by Hercynia, and it passed; the page records the cost as unknown. After the Winter Solstice 380YE, Llewellyn Leafstalker provided 5 wains of white granite and 10 crowns towards the work. The workshop was subsequently completed and stands in Holtford in Miaren.

n.Navarr: The Navarr territory of Miaren gained a completed alchemical workshop dedicated to Murit, built at the request of its own senator.

t.Miaren: Miaren's senator proposed the potion lab, and the workshop dedicated to Murit was duly built within the territory.

r.Miaren/Holtford: Holtford is the site of the completed alchemical workshop dedicated to Murit.

Construct Garden of the Grim II.d: Proposed by the senator for Miekarova and seconded by Volodmartz, the self-funded motion sought to create a herb sinecure titled "The Grim Gardener", with the holder to be appointed by the Senators of Varushka. It followed an earlier failed motion to build the same sinecure. Although the Senate passed it, the commission was announced only after the maximum number of commissions for the season had been authorised. It was held in reserve in case the Synod vetoed one of the earlier commissions. No veto was used, so the Gardens of the Grim commission was not authorised.

n.Varushka: Varushka's senators would have appointed the Grim Gardener, but because the commission was never authorised, the nation gained no new herb sinecure despite a second attempt.

t.Miekarova: The proposed Gardens of the Grim herb sinecure in Miekarova passed the Senate but was not authorised, so nothing was built there.

Construct Hall of the Krampus.d: The motion called for a hall for the Krampus to be constructed in Skarsind as a folly, following recent events. It passed in Winter 380YE. The cost was 13 wains of white granite and 26 crowns in labour, with three months needed to build. After the Winter Solstice 380YE, Irontide Vio provided both the granite and the crowns. The campaign outcome records that the Krampushall has been constructed in Skarsind.

n.Imperial Orcs: The Imperial Orcs, who held Skarsind, gained the Krampushall in their territory, a folly proposed by Skarsind's senator and honouring the Krampus.

t.Skarsind: Skarsind became home to the Krampushall, a folly for the Krampus built from white granite and crowns supplied by Irontide Vio.

Construct Home of the Broken Shield.d: Announced in Winter 380YE under the power to commission constructions delegated to the Civilian Commissioner by the Senate, the Home of the Broken Shield is a sinecure producing herbs, sited in Skogei's Glen in Skarsind. It costs 10 wains of weirwood and 20 crowns in labour, and takes three months to build. Bloodcrow Yargol provided the full weirwood and crowns after the Winter Solstice. Once completed, it will create a new Imperial Orc national title, Broken Shield Guardian. Certain necessary details still had to be settled before construction could begin.

n.Imperial Orcs: The Imperial Orcs gain a planned communal home for those of the Broken Shield and, once it is built, a new national title, Broken Shield Guardian, with Bloodcrow Yargol supplying the materials and labour costs.

t.Skarsind: The Home of the Broken Shield is to be built in Skogei's Glen, Skarsind, as a sinecure producing herbs, though some necessary details remained to be settled before work could start.

Construct Jarmish Docks.d: The senator for Kallavesa proposed the motion and the senator for Redoubt seconded it. It called for docks in Cargo, designed by the Asavean Architect, where weirwood could be bought from Jarm. Construction cost 15 wains of weirwood, 15 wains of white granite and 60 crowns in labour, and was to take three months. Olle Markusson supplied all of these after the Winter Solstice. The motion lacked some necessary details, which Senator Kallavesa was allowed to decide. Once completed, the docks created the title Prime Factor of the Pallas Docks.

n.Urizen: Urizen's territory of Redoubt gained a ministry for trading with Jarm for weirwood, and its senator seconded the motion that built it.

t.Redoubt: The Jarmish Weirwood docks were to be built at Cargo in Redoubt, giving the territory a ministry for buying weirwood from Jarm and, once complete, the new title Prime Factor of the Pallas Docks.

Construct Jarmish trade hub in Tassato.d: The motion, put forward by the senator for Tassato and seconded by the senator for Holberg, authorised a trade hub for merchants from the Principalities of Jarm who wanted access to the mana exchange in the city of Enterio. It passed in Winter 380YE. The cost is not recorded and was met by the Jarmish traders themselves rather than the Imperial treasury. The work was completed shortly before the Spring Equinox of 381YE, and the Jarmish traders now have a lodge in Enterio, Tassato.

n.The League: A League city gained a permanent foreign trading presence, with Jarmish merchants building and paying for their own lodge to reach Enterio's mana exchange.

t.Tassato: Tassato's senator proposed the motion, and the territory now hosts a lodge where Jarmish traders base their dealings with the mana exchange in Enterio.

r.Tassato/Enterio: The Jarmish lodge was built in the city of Enterio and finished shortly before Spring Equinox 381YE, giving Jarmish traders a base beside the city's mana exchange.

Construct Menagerie.d: Proposed by Morrow and seconded by Conscience, the motion was to be self-funded by the House of Seven Mirrors. The construction was costed at 3 wains of white granite, 2 wains of mithril and 10 crowns in labour, and would take three months; its progress was recorded as unknown. Once complete, it would create the Imperial title of Keeper of the Imperial Menagerie, a lifetime appointment made by the Throne and revocable by the General Assembly and the Assembly of Nine. The Keeper would care for the rakshasa and receive a regular income of Winter vis and 'Tears of the Rakshasa', a substance the creature produces when it is happy.

n.The League: The League was to host a new Imperial sinecure on its soil. The rakshasa it would house had already been given the name 'Flocki' by the children of Holberg.

t.Holberg: Holberg, held by the League, was chosen as the site of the Imperial Menagerie, which would house the Empress's tame rakshasa.

r.Holberg/Holmauer: Holmauer was the planned location of the menagerie, where the enclosure would be built from white granite and mithril over three months.

Construct Temple of the Way in Nemoria.d: Proposed by Feroz and seconded by Madruga, the motion passed at the Winter Solstice 380YE. Construction required 20 wains of white granite and 10 thrones in emancipated labour costs, and would take six months. After the solstice, Oria i Shartha i Riqueza provided both the granite and the money. Once the temple was completed, it created an Imperial title of liaison, charged with making sure the temple receives the liao it needs. In effect this was a ministry allowing liao to be traded for Asavean trade goods. After the Autumn Equinox 381YE it was settled that the Freeborn assembly would appoint the liaison by judgement, with the title available from the Winter Solstice 381YE.

n.The Brass Coast: A Freeborn senator proposed the temple and a Freeborn citizen, Oria i Shartha i Riqueza, paid for it. The resulting liaison title, which trades liao for Asavean goods, is appointed by the Freeborn assembly.

t.Feroz: The senator for Feroz proposed the motion that led to the Temple of the Way being built in Nemoria.

Construct The Wellspring of Jade.d: Acting under the power to commission constructions delegated to him by the Senate, the Civilian Commissioner of The League approved the building of a sinecure in Sarvos at standard cost, self-funded by Giacomo Corvinoscuro and Lorenzo La Volpe. After the Winter Solstice 380YE, Giacomo Corvinoscuro provided 16 wains of mithril and 4 thrones towards it. Once complete, the construction will create a new national title within the League related to the Jade Custodian. However, work could not begin until Lorenzo La Volpe set the region and production of the sinecure, which had not yet been done.

n.The League: The League stands to gain a new national title linked to the Jade Custodian once the sinecure is finished, commissioned by its own Civilian Commissioner and paid for by League citizens rather than the Senate treasury.

t.Sarvos: A sinecure, the Wellspring of Jade, was commissioned for the Sarvos countryside, though its exact region and production still had to be chosen before work could start.

Construct Vales Might.d: The Civilian Commissioner of Wintermark approved the construction of Vales Might using the power to commission constructions that the Senate had delegated to them. The sinecure is to produce crystal mana in Wood Heath, Hahnmark. It cost 12 wains of mithril and 3 thrones in labour, and was to take three months to build. Tyr Brenna provided the full 12 wains of mithril and 3 thrones after the Winter Solstice 380YE. Once completed, the construction will create a new national title within Wintermark, the Keeper of the Crystal Vale.

n.Wintermark: Wintermark's Civilian Commissioner commissioned the sinecure and Tyr Brenna funded it, and the nation will gain a new national title, the Keeper of the Crystal Vale, once it is built.

t.Hahnmark: Hahnmark, held by Wintermark, is to gain a new sinecure producing crystal mana once the three-month construction is complete.

r.Hahnmark/Wood Heath: Wood Heath is the site of Vales Might, a sinecure commissioned to produce crystal mana.

Construct cargo dock in Cargo.d: Proposed by Madruga and seconded by Segura, the motion called for a dock costing 10 white granite, 40 weirwood and 12 thrones 4 crowns in labour, taking three months to build. The materials and money were provided by Thanmir Hrafn after the Summer Solstice 381YE. Once complete, the dock creates the title Bewaarder van het Vandersaar dok, which works like a ministry and allows purchase of white granite from the Sarcophan Delves at 32 crowns a wain for the first 8 wains, 29 for the next 8 and 26 for the last 8. The title would normally be appointed through the Bourse. As a ministry it has no upkeep. Some details were left for Senator Madruga to decide.

n.Urizen: The dock was built in Redoubt, a Urizen territory, bringing a Sarcophan white granite trade route through Urizen lands at Cargo.

t.Redoubt: Redoubt was to gain a cargo dock at Cargo, creating the title Bewaarder van het Vandersaar dok and a way to buy up to 24 wains of white granite a season from the Sarcophan Delves.

Construct the Celesti Lighthouse II.d: Acting under the construction powers the Senate had delegated to them, the Civilian Commissioner of the Brass Coast commissioned works to renovate the lighthouse lantern in Oran, Feroz. This followed an earlier, unauthorised motion from Autumn 380YE. The project cost 16 wains of mithril and 4 thrones in labour and took three months to build. Ahraz i Guerra provided the mithril and thrones after the Winter Solstice. Once completed, it would create the ministry of the Keeper of the Celesti Lighthouse, a Freeborn national title appointed by the Brass Coast senators and empowered to purchase mana crystals from ship captains at rates set by the Civil Service.

n.The Brass Coast: The Freeborn gain a national ministry, the Celesti Lighthouse Keeper, appointed by their senators and able to buy mana from ship captains. The Brass Coast's Civilian Commissioner approved it and the Freeborn Ahraz i Guerra paid its costs.

t.Feroz: The lighthouse at Oran in Feroz has its lantern renovated and becomes the base of a ministry where mana crystals can be bought from visiting ship captains.

Construct the Eternal Flame of Miaren.d: The Civilian Commissioner of Navarr approved the construction of the Eternal Flame of Miaren, a sinecure in Seren, Miaren, that produces mana crystals. The commission cost 10 wains of mithril and 20 crowns in labour and was to take three months to build. Bronwyn Kane provided both the mithril and the crowns. Certain necessary details had to be settled before work could begin. Once completed, the construction created a new national title within Navarr, the Eternal Flame of Miaren.

n.Navarr: Navarr gained a new national title, the Eternal Flame of Miaren, commissioned by its own Civilian Commissioner and funded by Bronwyn Kane.

t.Miaren: The Eternal Flame was to be raised in Seren, Miaren, as a sinecure producing mana crystals.

Construct theatre in Temeschwar.d: Proposed by the senator for Temeschwar and seconded by Semmerholm, the motion commissioned a great work at a cost of 15 wains of white granite, 5 wains of weirwood, 5 thrones and three months of construction. All materials and money were provided by Lorenzo "La Volpe" Macelliao von Temeschwar after the Winter Solstice 380YE. The finished Bloody Great Theatre, completed shortly before the Spring Equinox 381YE, provides 15 liao and 30 votes in the Synod each season, shared among Temeschwar citizens dedicated to Pride who own congregations, following attendance at the Anvil Summit.

n.The League: League priests of Pride in Temeschwar who own congregations gain a seasonal share of 15 liao and 30 Synod votes from the new theatre, strengthening the League's religious voice.

t.Temeschwar: Temeschwar gained the Bloody Great Theatre, funded by Lorenzo "La Volpe" Macelliao von Temeschwar and completed shortly before the Spring Equinox 381YE as a celebration of the city's Pride.

Darkest night.d: Over roughly a year the starless night had spread across ten territories. It now covers all of the Empire, the former Imperial territories of Liathaven and the Mournwold, and Brocéliande. Skies look normal by day, but at night only the moon is visible. The stars' magic can still be felt. A magnitude forty-one Night shroud, detectable even by day, blocks lesser scrying such as Eyes of the Sun and Moon, Eye of the High Places and Dreams in the Witch House, for foreign magicians and eternals alike. Naga across the affected lands struggle to be open or honest. The Augurs of the Opalescent Gloaming of Hahnmark gave the Imperial Seer the Hawk's Demeanour mask and promised two doses of Waters of the Shimmering Shore.

n.Druj: The Barrens, held by the Druj, were among the first lands to lose their stars and remain under the shroud, which blocks attempts to scry them below magnitude forty-one.
n.Highguard: Highguard's Necropolis was already starless, and now Casinea and the rest of its lands are dark at night and shrouded against scrying.
n.Imperial Orcs: Skarsind, held by the Imperial Orcs, was one of the earliest territories swallowed by the Empty Skies and remains under the scrying-blocking shroud.
n.Jotun: The Jotun-held former Imperial territories of Liathaven and the Mournwold are now under the starless sky and shroud, making them very hard for anyone to scry, and naga there feel the urge to secrecy.
n.The Brass Coast: Segura was among the territories already darkened, and the Brass Coast's lands remain shrouded against scrying with no stars visible at night.
n.The League: Holberg was one of the first territories whose stars vanished, and the League's lands remain beneath the magnitude forty-one shroud.
n.The Marches: Bregasland had already lost its stars, and the Marches now sit wholly under the starless night and its scrying-blocking shroud.
n.Varushka: Volodmartz, Karsk and Miekarova were all among the earlier starless territories, leaving Varushka thoroughly shrouded against divination.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark's lands are shrouded, and the Winterfolk Augurs of the Opalescent Gloaming answered by gifting the Imperial Seer a magical mask and promising two doses of Waters of the Shimmering Shore.

t.Bregasland: Bregasland was among the territories already starless before the phenomenon spread, and it remains under the magnitude forty-one shroud.
t.Brocéliande: Though not an Imperial territory, Vallorn-held Brocéliande is now also covered by the starless sky and shroud, and the naga effect applies there.
t.Casinea: Casinea now falls under the starless night sky and the scrying-blocking shroud along with every other Imperial territory.
t.Hahnmark: Hahnmark is now shrouded and starless, and is home to the Augurs of the Opalescent Gloaming, who have made gifts to the Imperial Seer in response.
t.Holberg: Holberg was one of the earliest territories to lose its stars and remains shrouded against scrying below magnitude forty-one.
t.Karsk: Karsk had already lost its stars before the spread and remains under the shroud.
t.Liathaven: Jotun-held Liathaven, a former Imperial territory, is now included in the starless sky, the shroud and the naga effect.
t.Miekarova: Miekarova was among the territories already swallowed by the Empty Skies and remains shrouded against divination.
t.Mournwold: The Jotun-held Mournwold, a former Imperial territory, is now covered by the starless night and the shroud, and naga there feel driven to secrecy.
t.Necropolis: Necropolis was one of the earlier territories to lose its stars and remains beneath the magnitude forty-one shroud.
t.Segura: Segura had already gone starless before the spread and stays shrouded against scrying.
t.Sermersuaq: Sermersuaq was among the first territories to go starless and remains under the shroud.
t.Skarsind: Skarsind was among the territories already starless and continues under the shroud that impedes large-scale scrying.
t.The Barrens: The Druj-held Barrens were already starless, and the naga effect explicitly applies there along with the shroud.
t.Volodmartz: Volodmartz had already lost its stars before the phenomenon spread Empire-wide and remains shrouded.

r.Hahnmark/Kronemark: The Augurs of the Opalescent Gloaming are based at White Owl Hall on the icy shores of Lake Kronevann, from where they sent their gifts to the Imperial Seer.

Death of a salesman.d: The civil service's acquirers came back empty-handed, and no private auction would be held. Most acquirers were reassigned, and no remedy had been found. Five opportunities arose in its place. Iñes i Daero of the Saffron Sails would auction a long-hallowed fragment of Emperor Barabbas's flagship in the Freeborn camp. The orc bonesetter Whed sought Sunhammer Krag's help to sell a white tablet and letters found in Crow's Ridge. Basileus Flint offered two seasons' hire of the Shrouded spies, with the Grendel's sealed bid as the floor. The Red Maggots would sell the Black Garden, a Realmsroot-bearing estate in West Marsh. Escon called Highborn benefactors to hear funding appeals.

n.Grendel: Basileus Flint had already offered the Shrouded spies to the Grendel, and their sealed bid would set the minimum price at the Anvil auction. The relic for sale also recalled Barabbas's ill-fated fleet, which sailed against the Grendel in 199YE.
n.Highguard: Escon called wealthy Highborn to a benefactors' council in the Highborn camp. There the Heirs of Lepidus and the artisans of Esther's Forge would each seek investment in their work.
n.Imperial Orcs: The Imperial Orc bonesetter Whed bought a strange white tablet at the Torfast Trading Post. He planned to come to Anvil and ask overseer Sunhammer Krag to help him find a buyer.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: Liathaven, then held by the Jotun, is named as the homeland of the Navarr refugee Hywel, who died fighting there.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: the Black Garden estate had belonged to the Navarr thorn Hywel. He pawned it to the Red Maggots before falling in battle in Liathaven.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: an acquirer had been disappointed by the Carta Raisa in Tassato, and the Heirs of Lepidus had worked with Tassato's School of Epistemology.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: the letters found with the white tablet were correspondence from 160YE between a Kallavesi mystic and a Thule from Neeyukir about uncovering the past.
n.Wintermark: The Red Maggots would auction the Black Garden, a Kallavesi estate that yields herbs and Realmsroot, in the Wintermark camp. The garden was considered of primary interest to Wintermarkers.

t.Kallavesa: A deserted estate in Kallavesa, the Black Garden, was found overgrown with rare herbs and Realmsroot. Its new owners, the Red Maggots, put it up for sale.
t.Liathaven: Mentioned in passing: Hywel, the estate's former owner, was a refugee from Liathaven who died after rejoining the army to fight there.
t.Necropolis: Mentioned in passing: the artisans of Esther's Forge, who asked to address the benefactors' council, have their chapter house near Necropolis.
t.Skarsind: An orc hunting in Skarsind found the white tablet and its letters. He was driven off by angry Winterfolk but kept his find and sold it at the Torfast Trading Post.
t.Tassato: Mentioned in passing: the Carta Raisa in Tassato had disappointed a Bourse acquirer, and the city's School of Epistemology had helped the Heirs of Lepidus.

r.Kallavesa/West Marsh: The Black Garden lies half-sunk in West Marsh, its ruined stone estate overrun with herbs and Realmsroot. Locals rumoured that it was unsafe and close to regiones of Winter or Night.
r.Skarsind/Crow’s Ridge: The tablet, writing case and letters were found by a hunting orc in Crow's Ridge. Winterfolk there angrily drove him away from the area.

Disburse funds for rebuilding of Holmaue.d: The motion followed an earlier motion to disburse funds, which had itself come after a motion to construct a great work in Holberg. Proposed by the senator for Holberg and seconded by the senator for Tassato, it called for funds to be released for the rebuilding of Holberg. It passed at 75 thrones, and that sum was disbursed to the senator for Holberg.

n.The League: League senators for Holberg and Tassato proposed and seconded the motion, securing 75 thrones from the Imperial treasury for a League territory.

t.Holberg: The senator for Holberg received 75 thrones towards rebuilding in the territory, continuing an earlier great work effort there.

r.Holberg/Holmauer: Holmauer was the focus of the rebuilding effort that the 75 thrones were released to fund.

Fortify Reikos.d: The motion to fortify Reikos was proposed by the senator for Bastion and seconded by Upwold, and it passed in Winter 380YE. The fortification was to be built in Broken Ride and cost 160 wains of white granite and 45 thrones in labour, take 12 months to construct, and carry 12 thrones a year in upkeep. Brother Ibrahim the South Paw supplied 20 wains of white granite and 5 thrones after the Winter Solstice 380YE. Sammual of the Cohort of the Winter Bear then provided 40 wains and 7 thrones after the Spring Equinox 381YE, and 100 wains and 33 thrones after the Summer Solstice 381YE, which together met the full materials and labour costs.

n.Highguard: Bastion's senator proposed a fortification for Highguard's territory of Reikos. Highguard citizens and allies then supplied the granite and thrones needed to strengthen the defences of Broken Ride.

t.Reikos: Reikos was to gain a new fortification in Broken Ride, adding to the defences of the Highguard-held territory.

r.Reikos/Broken Ride: Broken Ride was chosen as the site of the new fortification, which was fully funded by Summer 381YE.

In brightest day.d: The enchantment drove artists to new heights and moved everyone to celebrate their nation's art, with a flourishing unseen since Empress Richilde. Until it faded, Hallowings of Richilde were two points stronger. The Senate could commission galleries, museums and performance spaces as great works costing 15 wains of white granite, 5 wains of weirwood and 5 Thrones in labour. Each would give 30 Synod votes and 15 liao to Pride congregations in its territory if finished before the Summer Solstice; otherwise it would be a folly. Civilian Commissioners could not build them. House Bourné revealed six raiment schemata, one for each realm, which any Imperial artisan could learn in Sarvos.

n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: Abraham of Bastion appears in the opening fiction, tackling his distracted comrade out of the path of a javelin.
n.Imperial Orcs: Kalpaheim was among the cities where art flourished, and Blackspear Tak features in the opening fiction, shielding his companions in battle.
n.The Brass Coast: Siroc saw a marked flowering of the arts, and the fiction recalls how Empress Richilde won over the Freeborn senators of the Erigo, Riqueza and Guerra with honest words.
n.The League: All four League cities saw an unprecedented artistic flourishing, and the Sarvosan House Bourné revealed six ritual-robe schemata through the League broadsheet The Looking Glass.
n.The Marches: Meade was named among the cities that saw a flowering of artistic expression and interest in the arts.
n.Wintermark: Even Gildenheim shared in the Empire-wide surge of artistic expression and pride in national art.

t.Bastion: Mentioned in passing: only through the name of Abraham of Bastion, a soldier in the opening fiction.
t.Hahnmark: Gildenheim was noted, perhaps surprisingly, as one of the cities where interest in the arts flourished.
t.Madruga: Siroc saw a marked flourishing of artistic expression under the enchantment's influence.
t.Mitwold: Meade was among the cities where the enchantment's effect on art and artists was particularly marked.
t.Sarvos: The city flourished artistically, and the wealthy guild House Bourné opened its estate to any Imperial artisan wishing to learn its six new raiment schemata.
t.Skarsind: Kalpaheim was named among the cities that saw an unprecedented flourishing of artistic expression.
t.Tassato: As one of the League's four cities it shared in the artistic flourishing, and the fiction recalls a play about Empress Richilde staged in a Tassato theatre.

Into the woods.d: Since the coldest night of the winter, spirits and wandering dead have been seen across Metri. Bandits, muggers and anyone intending violence are torn apart by gaunt figures who claim to serve the Prince of the Icy Heart and offer safe passage. Robbers have abandoned the region, and trade routes north to Skarsind and east to Karov have never been easier to travel. Yet people feel watched, and some are fleeing. At the Fortress of Salt mithril mine, a miner's heart was torn out during a brawl. Production continues, but the mood is strained. Metri has gained the haunted quality. Diviners doubt it is an enchantment but cannot be certain, and strange individuals have been asking after Tobias Shanks.

n.Imperial Orcs: Mentioned in passing: the trade route from Metri north to the Imperial Orc territory of Skarsind is named among those that have become unusually safe to travel.
n.The League: A League region in Temeschwar has become haunted, its roads now free of bandits but its people uneasy and some fleeing, while the Fortress of Salt's mithril output continues under a tense atmosphere.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: the trade route east from Metri to Karov has become safer, and the page closes with a traditional Varushkan tale about the woods.

t.Karov: Mentioned in passing: the road east from Metri to Karov is among the trade routes now unusually free of bandits.
t.Skarsind: Mentioned in passing: the trade route north from Metri to Skarsind has never been easier to travel.
t.Temeschwar: One of Temeschwar's regions has fallen under a haunting presence that kills anyone threatening violence, and some residents are fleeing Metri for the presumed safety of the rest of the territory.

r.Temeschwar/Metri: Metri gained the haunted quality, with spirits of the Prince of the Icy Heart slaying would-be robbers and brawlers, its roads made safe, and the Fortress of Salt mine still producing despite deep unease among its workers.

Lantern's light.d: The star's impact lit the night over Varushka and northern Dawn, was heard as far as Highguard, and was accompanied by scattered starfalls, some bearing small amounts of ilium. A Thule delegation came through Brez to the cabalists of Void and offered 4 rings of ilium each season, but only to a Varushkan and only while Varushka stays at peace with Otkodov. The warlock Rak invited the Empire to build an embassy, preferably Varushkan. Gar the Trader sought to join the Northern trade network, but Dogri Thulebane's control of the northern Skarsind passes blocked this. The Thule would not remove him without an invitation from the Senate.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: the night sky over parts of northern Dawn briefly blazed crimson-bright as the star fell.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: the sound of the star's impact was heard as far south as Highguard.
n.Imperial Orcs: Starfalls struck parts of Skarsind, and Thule trade through the Imperial Orc territory to Torfast was blocked by Dogri Thulebane's hold on its northern passes. Gar regretted losing the chance to learn more about the Imperial Orcs.
n.Thule: The Thule honoured their agreement by sharing the star metal from Sküld with Varushka, sought a Varushkan-run embassy, and hoped to join the Northern trade network. They would not move against Dogri in Skarsind without an invitation from the Senate.
n.Varushka: Varushka alone was offered the ilium share for keeping faith with the Thule, and gained it as the national Bourse seat Gift of the Dwindling Star, held so long as it stays at peace with Otkodov. The Thule also favoured a Varushkan embassy.
n.Wintermark: Burning rock fell on parts of northern Wintermark, and the stubborn Winterfolk following Dogri Thulebane held the Skarsind passes against the Thule.

t.Karsk: Mentioned in passing: Ivarsgard in Karsk was one of the Thule's suggested sites for the ilium trade offices.
t.Miekarova: The pillar of ash from the impact was visible for hours across Miekarova, and Wendell's Hope was suggested as a possible site for the ilium offices.
t.Otkodov: The red star struck eastern Otkodov and left a significant deposit of star metal. The ilium trade depends on Varushka remaining at peace with the territory.
t.Sermersuaq: Dogri Thulebane's control of the routes from Silver Peaks helped deter the Thule from sending caravans south.
t.Skarsind: Starfalls struck parts of Skarsind, and Dogri Thulebane's 'Skarsind congregation of Loyalty' held the northern passes, violently turning back Thule orcs surveying a road.
t.Volodmartz: The ash pillar was visible across Volodmartz, and the Thule delegation came to Void in Brez, where the new ilium offices were established.

r.Miekarova/Mieriada: Mentioned in passing: Wendell's Hope in Miekarova was among the Thule's suggested sites for the ilium offices; the page does not name Mieriada itself.
r.Otkodov/Sküld: The red star slammed into Sküld, creating the star metal deposit the Thule chose to share with Varushka.
r.Sermersuaq/Silver Peaks: Mentioned in passing: Dogri Thulebane's control of the routes from Silver Peaks was cited as a reason the Thule would not risk caravans south.
r.Skarsind/Southpine: Mentioned in passing: the page refers only to the northern Skarsind passes held by Dogri Thulebane and does not name Southpine.
r.Volodmartz/Brez: The Thule delegation came down through the mountains of Brez to the cabalists of Void, where Rak was hosted and where the Gift of the Dwindling Star's offices were established.

Missionary work.d: A Senate motion by Senator Avisena i Kharizmi i Guerra of Segura asked the Synod to make missionaries available to anyone in the Iron Confederacy willing to receive them. The Dukes and Suranni citizens gave no formal response. However, a representative of several hundred rebels, mostly escaped human slaves camped in the hills of Kalino, sought out the civil service. They wanted teaching on the Way and auras of Courage and Loyalty to help their struggle. The General Assembly could send a priest with liao to support the rebellion, or one to persuade the rebels to seek sanctuary in the Empire. During the Winter Solstice the Empress intervened, both mandates failed to reach the Greater Majority, and Kalino was left to unfold without Imperial involvement.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: a civil servant tells the rebel envoys that the Empire's nobles will be camping with the Dawnish.
n.Imperial Orcs: Mentioned in passing: a group of Imperial Orcs walking by at Anvil frightens one of the rebel envoys.
n.The Brass Coast: A Brass Coast senator from Segura raised the motion that opened this opportunity, and the rebels' camp lies just south of the Brass Coast's border at Feroz, but the Synod's failure to act meant no Imperial help reached them.

t.Feroz: Mentioned in passing: Kalino, where the rebels are camped, is described as lying south of Feroz.
t.Kalino: Several hundred escaped slaves camped in the hills of Kalino sought Imperial missionaries to aid their rebellion against the Suranni, but with both Synod mandates failing, events there continue without Imperial intervention.
t.Segura: Mentioned in passing: the motion offering missionaries to the Iron Confederacy was raised by Senator Avisena i Kharizmi i Guerra of Segura.

No evil shall escape our sight.d: Founded under Emperor Nicovar as an investigative arm of the Vigilance Assembly, the Silent Bell kept operating after being disbanded and has a mixed reputation for both uncovering threats and discrediting political movements. Its preceptor, Malachai, proposed that the Council of Nine direct its investigations by statement of principle, or alternatively by greater majority let it report privately to the Cardinal of Vigilance. The sodality insisted on staying apolitical and would not investigate threats whose primary source lies at Anvil. The Synod could endorse or reject it. It endorsed the sodality, and Esau the Highborn executed a supporting mandate, bringing improved attendance at Vigilance congregations across the Empire.

n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: a Grendel Salt Lord is used as an example of a foreign figure the Silent Bell would struggle to gather intelligence about directly.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: the Highborn Esau executed the mandate supporting the Silent Bell, which boosted Vigilance congregations across the Empire.

t.Casinea: Mentioned in passing: the Silent Bell's current preceptor, Malachai, is styled as being in Casca's Doom.

r.Casinea/Casfall: Mentioned in passing: the Silent Bell's preceptor, Malachai, is named as Malachai of the Silent Bell, in Casca's Doom.

Research Apaayuqiu King.d: Ioseph, the Minister for Historical Research, used the power to approve historical research delegated by the Senate to commission an inquiry into Apaayuqiu King and the pre-Wintermark history of the Sermersuaq area. He was particularly interested in a chain of bronze that marked her status as chief of chiefs. The request apparently followed a past-life vision experienced by Asenath of Felix Watch. The research cost 5 Thrones, which Ioseph of Phoenix Reach provided after the Winter Solstice 380YE. The civil service will compile research reports and present them to the Minister for Historical Research.

n.Wintermark: The research looks into history from before Wintermark, in lands Wintermark now holds. It may shed light on Apaayuqiu King and the bronze chain that marked her as chief of chiefs.

t.Sermersuaq: Sermersuaq is the focus of the inquiry, which examines the area's pre-Wintermark past and the chieftain Apaayuqiu King who once held authority there.

Serpent's tooth.d: After two earlier overtures failed, the Druj sent a third, unusually ordinary-seeming delegation, arranged to arrive at 11pm on the summit's first night. Their proposed terms: Murderdale and the Carmine Fields relinquished to them as traditional Barrens orc homelands, Dawn keeping Dawnguard and Drycastle; Fangs mithril traded for white granite (27 wains initially, up to 18 a season), though such trade is illegal while at war and would need a Senate motion and Bourse position; staged mutual army withdrawals; and the Great Forest orcs driven from Therunin. They sought at least five years of peace and stressed flexibility. Only the Senate could authorise a treaty, with the Imperial Consul expected to negotiate.

n.Dawn: Dawn was offered recognition of its hold on Dawnguard and Drycastle, but would have to surrender Murderdale and the Carmine Fields and reduce its presence to a single army at the Towers of the Dawn.
n.Druj: The Druj sent a high-ranking Tepel to bargain for Barrens lands they call orc homelands, offering mithril trade, staged withdrawal of their armies and a peace of five years or more.
n.Navarr: The Druj proposed that the Great Forest orcs be expelled from Navarri Therunin, either by the Empire or by two Druj armies that would then return to the Barrens.

t.The Barrens: The proposed treaty would partition the Barrens, ceding Murderdale and the Carmine Fields to the Druj while Dawn kept Dawnguard, with armies on both sides withdrawn over time and Fangs mithril potentially traded.
t.Therunin: Under the Druj terms the Great Forest orcs would be driven out of Therunin and resettled in the Barrens, possibly by two Druj armies entering the territory.

r.The Barrens/Dawnguard: The Druj offered to accept Dawnish control of Dawnguard and Drycastle, a return to the long-standing status quo.
r.The Barrens/Murderdale: The Druj demanded Murderdale be relinquished to them, with an army cautiously advancing to occupy it if terms were agreed.

Symposium of Revelation.d: Watcher secured a General Assembly judgement that invited speakers would not count as preaching under the laws on blasphemy, idolatry and heresy. This was widely read as a signal that religious crimes at the Symposium would not be prosecuted. The Symposium had no formal powers. Sessions ran from 2pm to 8:30pm and covered Exemplars, Yael's Revelation, the realms and Eternals, the Eternal Schism, true and false virtues, and orcs and the Howling Abyss. Assemblies invited foreign guests. Grendel, Axou, Faradene, Sarcophan, Jarmish and Commonwealth representatives were confirmed or expected. Asavean priests, the Lasambrian orcs, the Eternal Roshanwe and the Sumaah Republic remained uncertain.

n.Grendel: Although at war with the Empire, the Grendel accepted the League assembly's invitation and confirmed they would send a spiritual representative, apparently eager to educate the Synod about the true virtues.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: Highguard is not named directly on the page, and its people may only have taken part in the Symposium's debates on the Way like any other Imperial priests.
n.Imperial Orcs: The newly formed Imperial Orc national assembly played an active part. Bonewall Rek invited a Commonwealth delegation, Cardinal Atla invited the Sumaah Republic, and Imperial Orc preachers convened a panel on orcs, the Howling Abyss and their place in the doctrine of the Way.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: the Lasambrian orcs were said to have left the Empire to join or ally with the Jotun, and the invitation to them was noted as not meant for the Jotun who hold western Lasambria.
n.The Brass Coast: Danita i Riqueza and the Brass Coast national assembly invited the priests of Faraden, and at least one Faradene priest was expected, possibly to seek the return of the Copper Scrolls. Immeldar of the Freeborn assembly also invited the Lasambrian orcs, without reply.
n.Urizen: Belisarius and the Urizen national assembly invited their Axou "cousins", and despite Axos's usual reticence on religion, a priest was confirmed as travelling to present at the Symposium.

t.Feroz: Mentioned in passing: several Asavean priests invited to the Symposium were already in the Empire working on the Temple of Balo and the Black Bull in Feroz.
t.Necropolis: Mentioned in passing: Necropolis is not named on the page, and the Symposium took place in Anvil rather than in the territory.

Tale of the Golden Hare.d: At Spring Equinox the Fellowship of the Tangled Thorns was inquisited by Ula Ulanya Ulanaya of the Vigilance Assembly over blasphemy, idolatry and heresy; the assembly declined to castigate them. At Autumn Equinox Hubert Gremani passed a statement that the executed coven members were good and virtuous Varushkans. In defiant sympathy, Varushkans painted golden hares on signs, wore hare buckles and considered the less fortunate, though nobody agreed what the hare symbolised and some ideas bordered on heresy. The assembly could ignore it, name it a virtuous animal or denounce it as an idol. Hubert Gremani led a mandate naming the hare a symbol of Ambition; Esrys added a statement that revering or worshipping the golden hare remains idolatrous.

n.Varushka: Varushkans embraced the golden hare in memory of the Tangled Thorns, and their national assembly settled the matter by declaring the hare a symbol of Ambition while warning that worshipping it is idolatry.

t.Miekarova: Miekarova, where the Tangled Thorns were largely based and Dušan Otecovna Zlata had served as senator, was a centre of the discussion that led vales to take up the golden hare.

The Witches of Applefell.d: Two large bandit groups, many of them witches using spells to scatter guards and empower warriors, attacked a weirwood shipment heading south from the Weirwater Vales. They took five wains of weirwood, wagons and oxen, and left guards seriously injured. Evidence points to Applefell, but its yeofolk will not cooperate, and the witches' purpose for the weirwood is unknown. The new holder of the Weirwater Vales, auctioned at the Winter Solstice, will receive only 18 wains and may lose future production. An anonymous informant offered to sell information to the new holder at the auction. A general in Weirwater could issue the Leave no stone unturned order to end the bandit threat for at least a year, at the risk of fighting poorly if attacked.

n.Dawn: The theft of weirwood from a Dawnish territory, and the uncooperative and possibly subverted yeofolk of Applefell, left Dawn facing a witch-backed brigand problem that a Dawnish general could tackle with the Leave no stone unturned order.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: troubadours suggest Applefell's yeofolk have Varushkan blood, and Weirwater's wilds are compared with the more dangerous Varushkan wilderness.

t.Karov: Mentioned in passing: merchants passing through Applefell travel to and from Karov.
t.Semmerholm: The emboldened bandits have been reported making occasional attacks across the border into Semmerholm, a destination for merchants passing through Applefell.
t.Weirwater: Witch-supported bandits based around Applefell robbed the Weirwater Vales of five wains of weirwood. An army in the territory could be ordered to sweep its hills and forests to end the threat for at least a year, at the cost of fighting badly if attacked.

r.Weirwater/Hawksmoor: Mentioned in passing: Hawksmoor is not named on the page and is attached only as part of Weirwater, where the bandits and witches operate.
r.Weirwater/Sandling: Bandits have been reported attacking along the edges of Sandling as their raids grow bolder.
r.Weirwater/Weirmoor: Mentioned in passing: Applefell's yeofolk are more worried about the army of unliving horrors in Weirmoor than about the bandits, and the unliving forces in western Weirwater are a risk to any army hunting brigands.
r.Weirwater/Wickmoor: Bandits have been reported attacking along the edges of Wickmoor as their raids grow bolder.

The widening gyre.d: After nearly a year of impasse at Crows Keep, Dogri's warriors turned back Thule traders at Crows Ridge; a fight left one Wintermarker and all the Thule dead. Dogri refused to hand anyone over to an Imperial Orc magistrate, saying he would yield only to a Wintermark army. A raid would not break the Thule peace treaty but would bring reparations proportional to its size. Captains could covertly support the raid with military units; any Imperial army could occupy Crows Ridge and arrest him, with casualties, though a Wintermark army could do so bloodlessly. Alternatively, leaking his target to the Thule would see him destroyed and improve relations, or the Senate could cede Crows Ridge to the Thule.

n.Imperial Orcs: Crows Ridge in their territory of Skarsind was effectively outside their control, and their magistrate was turned away; betraying Dogri to the Thule or arresting him would let them resume full control of Skarsind.
n.Thule: Thule traders were killed at Crows Ridge and their lands faced a planned raid, for which they could demand weregild; if warned of the target they could ambush Dogri, and they could even be offered Crows Ridge by the Senate.
n.Wintermark: A Wintermark war hero from Britta's day was in open defiance, seeking support from like-minded Wintermarkers, and he would submit only to a Wintermark general, offering a Wintermark army the chance to arrest him without bloodshed.

t.Otkodov: If Dogri were betrayed to the Thule, the resulting thaw in relations would open new opportunities for trade with Otkodov in rare materials and rituals.
t.Skarsind: Dogri held Crows Keep and Crows Ridge in Skarsind as a rebel stronghold where the killings occurred; an Imperial army could occupy the area to end his defiance, or the Senate could cede Crows Ridge to the Thule.

Those who worship.d: The temple had been delayed by opposition from Abaddon de Rondell and the Assembly of the Nine and ran over time and budget, but only finishing work remained. Once complete it would improve relations with Asavea, and the Asaveans would appoint an Imperial liaison guided by the Senator for Feroz. A temple of the Way in Nemoria could then begin, needing 20 wains of white granite and either 10 Thrones or the Joãon family's slave labour. The Synod endorsed the Nemorian temple, mandating Lucifaro to use liao to encourage missionaries there. The Asavean priest Almodin Oktístis offered to oversee two large Senate commissions a season for 8 Thrones, and the Senate agreed to pay his stipend.

n.The Brass Coast: Freeborn Oran hosts the new Asavean temple, a Freeborn senator's earlier motion underpins the planned temple in Nemoria, and Almodin Oktístis, who had grown fond of the Brass Coast and worked closely with Freeborn architects and builders, was retained by the Senate.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: the Urizen priest Solas had attempted a veto that very nearly ended the temple project before it began.

t.Feroz: The temple of Balo and the Black Bull nears completion in Oran, and the Senator for Feroz will guide the Asavean choice of the Imperial liaison to its priests, a role offering access to Asavean goods.
t.Kahraman: Mentioned in passing: Maher i Zaydan i Riqueza, who raised the original temple motion as Senator for Kahraman, is expected by the Asaveans to oversee the Nemorian temple and decide how its title is appointed.

r.Feroz/Oranseri: In the port of Oran the Asavean temple's structure is finished, and three months of decoration and furnishing should see it offering services to Asavean sailors by the Spring Equinox.
